analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials specialist call: DAL, cruise
key_insights: Industrials closed up 30bps on 10/8 and materials rose with crude up 60bps, both outperforming the broader market. Energy and staples led, healthcare and technology lagged.
By subsector, transports, autos and housing led. Data center related names and airlines were lower. Large caps outperformed while beta moved sharply lower.
EQPT closed down 11% after another short report surfaced. GD closed up 1% after announcing a CEO transition that was planned but earlier than expected.

DAL reports Q3 on 10/9 pre-market. Expectations are 16-17% RASM growth for Q3, accelerating closer to 20% in Q4, with EPS more or less in line. The desk thinks investors are net long with a positioning score of 6-7/10.

US S&P futures are sharply higher led by technology after OpenAI put out year-end revenue targets ahead of expectations, which eased recent AI slowing fears. AAPL is falling pre-market on reports of order cuts.
Overseas, HSI is up 179bps and Europe is strong, led by Germany up 125bps after the region doubled its growth forecasts on construction strength.
Crude is down 100bps, with Brent at $103 and WTI at $90. European gas is down 2% to $78. The 10-year yield is 5.25%, off recent highs. DXY is $102 and Bitcoin is up 1% to $82.6k.
RTX won a five-year contract of up to $6.3bn for SM-3 IB interceptors and a $4.4bn Missile Defense Agency contract action for Standard Missile 3 block IB.
Yaskawa fell 5% overseas. The quarter was more or less in line but it cut its operating income forecast.
SPCX is weighing on communications names pre-market after announcing a deal with Spectrum for Mobile Services.

GIR (Lizzie) is constructive on cruise into earnings, citing accelerating consumer demand. CCL's 3Q results and bookings commentary and NCLH's positive pre-announcement point to improving demand across all geographies.
GIR expects the cruise competitive environment to reach an inflection point as supply growth moderates, comparisons ease and demand improves, setting up a strong year end and 2027.

GIR expects RCL to beat 3Q net yield guidance by about 80bps and to flow the beat through to a modest raise of FY net yield guidance, with core fundamental improvement more than offsetting fuel headwinds.

GIR keeps RCL at Buy: a clean beat-and-raise setup into 2H and 2027, net yield growth accelerating in 2027 versus 2026, and a potential positive catalyst from Perfect Day Mexico at an attractive valuation entry point.
